topic: IRP 2025 determination: 4.6 GW battery storage, storage as a timing asset
text:
On 7 October the energy minister issued the first procurement determination under IRP 2025: 9.6 GW of new capacity, of which 4.6 GW is battery storage and 5 GW is gas-to-power. There is no new wind or solar in this round.

The stated reason is curtailment. Renewable energy is increasingly being generated at times the grid cannot absorb it. The constraint is no longer only how much energy the country has, but when it has it.

That shift matters well beyond utility-scale projects. The same logic applies at the meter of a factory, cold store or shopping centre:
— solar yield that cannot be used on site has little value
— energy shifted from off-peak into peak periods on a time-of-use tariff can carry real value
— backup is now a secondary benefit, not the primary case

When we size storage for C&I clients, the first question is not how many hours of backup are needed. It is how the site's load profile lines up with its tariff periods.

National policy has now reached the same conclusion: storage is a timing asset.

For those planning C&I projects for 2027, is storage now part of the base case, or still an optional extra?
